question: A researcher wants to study how nurses feel about working night shifts by having open conversations. Which data collection method is best?

question: Which type of fever stays consistently high all day with almost no drops?

question: A patient sees a nurse open a pre-used syringe pack but says nothing. What is the main reason for this silence?

question: What does human factors engineering mainly look at in a hospital setting?

question: When is emergency surgery absolutely necessary for a patient with a small intestinal problem?

question: Why is writing accurate and prompt notes so crucial in an intensive care setting?

question: What special type of room ventilation is a must-have for patients on airborne precautions?

question: What is the primary calming chemical messenger (inhibitory neurotransmitter) targeted by most sleeping pills?

options.A: Dopamine
options.B: Norepinephrine
options.C: Acetylcholine
options.D: Gamma-aminobutyric acid

question: How do infectious germs from hospital waste most commonly find their way into a nurse's body?

options.A: Through accidental skin punctures or mucosal contact
options.B: Through breathing standard room air in patient wards
options.C: Through unbroken skin during routine ward cleaning
options.D: Through eating properly cooked hospital cafeteria food

explanation: Whenever there's a break in the skin (like a needle prick) or a splash into the eyes or mouth, germs in blood and body fluids get an open doorway straight into your body. [learn more](GST114_U6_T9#GST114_U6_T9_h2)

question: A patient had her right fallopian tube removed three years ago due to a severe infection. How is this absence classified?

question: What is the main purpose of monitoring and evaluation in post-abortion care programs?

options.A: To restrict patient access to modern contraceptive methods

question: What does an autoclave mainly use to achieve full sterilization?

options.A: Dry scorching hot air
options.B: Toxic formaldehyde gas

question: What is the leading cause of heavy bleeding right after childbirth (early postpartum hemorrhage)?

options.A: High blood pressure
options.B: Excessive walking
options.C: Vitamin deficiency
options.D: Uterine atony

question: What is the primary objective of tertiary prevention?

options.A: Promoting healthy lifestyle habits in children
options.B: Screening healthy populations for early signs
options.C: Limiting disability and restoring function
options.D: Stopping initial exposure to a disease agent

explanation: Tertiary prevention focuses on managing existing chronic conditions to prevent complications and maximize remaining abilities. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T4#GNS225_U2_T4_h4)

question: Which type of health need is decided by healthcare professionals using expert standards?

options.D: Comparative need

explanation: You got it! "Normative" comes from norms or standards. These are the needs experts spot based on professional guidelines and research. [learn more](GNS124_U3_T2#GNS124_U3_T2_h2)

question: A patient stands up fast and feels dizzy. What is the nurse likely suspecting?

options.B: Acute hypoglycemia

options.D: Orthostatic hypotension

question: What simple tool do nurses use to quickly spot acute malnutrition in toddlers?

question: What is the main job of a research hypothesis?

question: What is the tongue's main job right at the start of swallowing food?

question: What does the 'T' stand for in the TNM cancer staging system?

question: How do traditional healthcare systems generally view the concept of healing?

explanation: Spot on! Traditional systems look at the whole person—including their spiritual wellbeing and community ties—rather than just physical symptoms. [learn more](GNS314_U4_T2#GNS314_U4_T2_h1)

question: What type of question is best for encouraging a patient to talk freely during a health counselling session?

question: A patient with acute diarrhoea has sore, red skin around their bottom. What is the best immediate nursing step?

question: A patient develops severe depression after losing their job and home. Which category best describes these environmental and poverty stresses?

question: What is a major limitation of experimental research in busy hospitals?

question: How do the kidneys respond when a patient develops metabolic acidosis?

question: What was the core belief of the Moral Treatment movement?

question: A pregnant woman at 38 weeks gestation has a single baby lying head-down and normal blood pressure. Is she a candidate for home delivery?

question: Which blood test is commonly checked to assess a patient's nutrition before surgery?

question: Which type of life event is most likely to lead to complicated grief?

question: Who is primarily responsible for creating strategic plans in a healthcare organization?

question: What is the primary danger of filling a waste collection bag to the absolute brim?

question: Which method involves a nurse driving or walking through an area to observe living conditions firsthand?

question: When someone pushes back against your advocacy campaign, which of these should you NOT do?

question: Why do hospital leaders or administrators sometimes push back against health advocacy efforts?

question: What is the most important thing a nurse checks first during a cholera outbreak?

question: A patient on heparin suddenly has a very low platelet count and a new leg clot. What is going on?

question: What is the main job of glucose inside Oral Rehydration Salts (ORS)?

question: Which of the following conditions is a classic example of a metabolic crisis in diabetes?

question: Which tool is best used during a participatory needs assessment?

question: Why are fat-soluble vitamin supplements more likely to cause toxicity than water-soluble ones?

question: What is the main job of first-pass metabolism in the liver?

question: What is the main reason we group and organize medical supplies in a ward?

question: What is the name of the medication commonly used to treat an unruptured ectopic pregnancy medically?

question: Why do healthcare workers say the line between 'natural' and 'man-made' disasters is often blurry?

question: Which of the following is a simple, effective home method to make unsafe drinking water safer?

question: What is a major role of Community Health Workers in maternal and child health?

question: What is a major focus of modern molecular microbiology?

question: Why should a nurse read an ECG using a step-by-step routine?

question: Even though prolactin is high during pregnancy, why doesn't heavy milk production start right away?

question: Which vaccine is given in adolescent health programs to protect against cervical cancer later in life?

question: Why is good lighting so important when checking a patient's skin?

question: In infection control, what do we mean by the 'source of infection'?

question: How is chronic urinary retention different from acute urinary retention?

question: When you help a patient improve their nutrition knowledge, what practical skill does it usually help them master?

question: You just finished giving an elderly patient a bed bath. How should you dry their skin safely?

question: Which chemical messenger do anticholinergic drugs block in the bladder?

question: Which of these actions is NOT safe when handling medical waste?

question: What is the main reason for investigating a medication error on the ward?

question: What is the main goal of sex therapy when treating sexual dysfunction?

question: Why is spotting early warning signs so important in a relapse prevention plan?

options.C: It holds the Z-lines firmly in place during movement
options.D: It destroys excess acetylcholine in the synapse

explanation: At rest, tropomyosin blocks the binding sites like a locked door. Calcium acts as the key that shifts it out of the way so the muscle can get to work! [learn more](GNS121_U3_T12#GNS121_U3_T12_h5)

question: Why do nurse researchers need to know the different tiers of literature sources?

options.A: To ensure that every single source used is an unpublished thesis
options.B: To guarantee that only historical textbooks are cited in the study
options.C: To eliminate the need for peer-reviewed journal articles entirely
options.D: To build a strong argument and avoid weak or biased data

explanation: Spot on! Knowing your source tiers helps you pick reliable evidence to back up your nursing care and assignments. [learn more](GNS217_U3_T6#GNS217_U3_T6_h1)

question: Why does a high fever place extra stress on the heart?

options.A: Red blood cells stop carrying oxygen during a fever.
options.B: The heart muscle weakens from direct bacterial invasion.
options.C: The body's increased metabolic rate forces the heart to beat faster and work harder.
options.D: Blood pressure drops to dangerously low levels immediately.

explanation: Think of your body like an engine running hot: when you have a fever, your metabolic rate speeds up, meaning your heart has to pump faster to supply all that extra oxygen! [learn more](GNS221_U3_T3#GNS221_U3_T3_h5)

question: What is the main danger when a nurse transcribes (copies) a medication order?

options.A: It removes the need for nurses to check patient identity
options.B: It makes doctors write prescriptions much slower than usual
options.C: It permanently deletes previous medication history from the chart
options.D: It introduces opportunities for human error and misinterpretation

explanation: Spot on! Every time an order is manually copied over, there's a risk that numbers, decimals, or abbreviations might be misread. [learn more](GNS125_U2_T8#GNS125_U2_T8_h6)

question: A nurse wants to find out the percentage of pregnant women at a clinic who sleep less than five hours a night. Which design fits best?

options.A: Experimental design
options.B: Randomized controlled trial
options.C: Ex post facto design
options.D: Descriptive design

explanation: Brilliant! When you are just counting or checking the frequency of a habit or symptom in a group without testing a new drug or treatment, you are doing a descriptive study. [learn more](GNS224_U1_T8#GNS224_U1_T8_h2)

question: How should a nurse position a patient experiencing Superior Vena Cava Syndrome to help ease their symptoms?

options.A: Flat on their back with no pillow
options.B: With their legs raised higher than their head
options.C: On their left side in the recovery position
options.D: Upright with the head elevated

explanation: Keeping the head of the bed elevated uses gravity to help reduce venous pressure and swelling in the head and neck. [learn more](GNS321_U1_T13#GNS321_U1_T13_h6)

question: If the parasite travels to the wrong part of the body (ectopic infection), which system causes the most serious complications?

options.A: Central nervous system
options.B: Upper urinary tract
options.C: Peripheral vascular network
options.D: Musculoskeletal joints

explanation: Exactly! If the parasite wanders into the brain or spinal cord, it can lead to neurological issues and seizures, which is very serious. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T26#GNS313_U2_T26_h7)

question: A patient is fighting a bad malaria infection. Which food group should you encourage to boost their immune system?

options.A: Body-building foods like large amounts of table salt
options.B: Energy-giving foods like pure sugar and palm oil
options.C: Protective foods like oranges and spinach
options.D: Non-perishable foods like canned dry biscuits

explanation: Spot on! Fruits and veggies are 'protective' because their vitamins and minerals boost immunity and help the body fight off infections. [learn more](GNS227_U1_T007#GNS227_U1_T007_h3)

question: How do compulsions usually help a patient dealing with this condition?

options.A: They are physical exercises prescribed to improve general body tone
options.B: They serve as temporary relief from the anxiety caused by obsessions
options.C: They are creative hobbies used to express hidden artistic talents
options.D: They help the patient hallucinate pleasant images to pass the time

explanation: You got it! Compulsions are the repeated actions patients feel forced to do just to calm down the heavy anxiety sparked by their obsessions. [learn more](GNS314_U2_T7#GNS314_U2_T7_h1)

question: What is the primary goal of palliative care in a geriatric setting?

options.A: Finding a complete cure for terminal chronic illnesses
options.B: Improving quality of life and managing comfort and symptoms
options.C: Eliminating the need for family visits during illness
options.D: Speeding up the dying process to save facility resources

explanation: Palliative care focuses entirely on comfort, dignity, and easing pain so the resident can live their final days with peace. Beautiful nursing concept! [learn more](GNS324_U5_T13#GNS324_U5_T13_h7)

question: Which of the following is NOT a helpful way to encourage eating in a frail older adult?

options.A: Forcing the patient to finish large meals within a strict time limit
options.B: Ensuring dentures are clean and placed in the mouth before mealtime
options.C: Creating a quiet, pleasant environment free from clinical distractions
options.D: Offering frequent small meals and nutrient-dense snacks throughout the day

explanation: You got it! Forcing big meals on someone with a poor appetite can be overwhelming. Smaller, frequent plates and a calm atmosphere work wonders instead! [learn more](GNS227_U2_T014#GNS227_U2_T014_h6)

question: Which test is mainly used to check electrical brain waves and diagnose seizures?

options.A: Computed tomography (CT) scan
options.B: Intracranial pressure monitor
options.C: Electroencephalogram (EEG)
options.D: Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI)

explanation: An EEG places tiny sensors on the scalp to record brain electrical activity, making it the go-to test for seizure disorders. [learn more](GNS222_U3_T2#GNS222_U3_T2_h8)

question: Which of these actions is NOT a way nurses help prevent healthcare-associated infections?

options.A: Prescribing strong antibiotic medications to every new patient
options.B: Changing surgical wound dressings according to hospital policy
options.C: Using sterile technique during invasive urinary catheter insertions
options.D: Practicing consistent hand hygiene before and after patient contact

explanation: Spot on! Nurses don't prescribe drugs, and giving antibiotics to everyone would cause dangerous drug resistance rather than stop infections. Good catch! [learn more](GNS122_U2_T2#GNS122_U2_T2_h7)

question: Which of the following is an example of non-verbal communication?

options.A: Giving spoken instructions over the phone
options.B: Reading a printed pamphlet out loud
options.C: Using medical jargon during a lecture
options.D: Body posture and facial expressions

explanation: Non-verbal communication involves physical cues like body language, posture, and facial expressions rather than spoken words. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T22#GNS225_U2_T22_h3)

question: Which cells are the star players in our adaptive (targeted) immune response?

options.A: Adipocytes
options.B: Platelets
options.C: Lymphocytes
options.D: Erythrocytes

explanation: B cells and T cells are types of lymphocytes. They are the smart cells that handle the targeted, long-term memory side of immunity. [learn more](GST114_U4_T6#GST114_U4_T6_h3)

question: Which family planning pill is best for mothers who are breastfeeding in the early months because it won't dry up their milk?

options.A: Menopausal hormone therapy
options.B: Combined estrogen pills
options.C: High-dose emergency pills
options.D: Progestin-only pills

explanation: Progestin-only pills (the 'minipill') are safe for nursing moms because they don't mess with breastmilk production like estrogen can. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T52#GNS214_U1_T52_h8)

question: Which phrase is an example of unhelpful communication when talking to a dying patient?

options.A: "It is okay to cry and feel upset right now."
options.B: "Everything is going to be completely fine."
options.C: "I am right here with you through this."
options.D: "Tell me more about what you are feeling today."

explanation: False reassurances dismiss the patient's real fears and isolate them from honest conversation. [learn more](GNS321_U4_T16#GNS321_U4_T16_h5)

question: Why does high national debt servicing negatively affect public health budgets?

options.A: It directly increases the number of patients seeking private insurance
options.B: It forces international health organizations to withdraw all nursing staff
options.C: It automatically lowers the market price of essential pharmaceutical drugs
options.D: It drains government revenue that could otherwise be allocated to social sectors like health

explanation: When a huge chunk of national income goes to paying off debts, less money is left in the purse for hospitals, schools, and health programs. [learn more](GST322_U3_T2#GST322_U3_T2_h5)

question: When does the first stage of labour officially come to an end?

options.A: When regular uterine contractions first begin
options.B: When the baby's head emerges from the vagina
options.C: When the placenta is successfully delivered
options.D: When the cervix is fully dilated at 10 centimeters

explanation: Stage one is all about opening the cervix. Once it hits 10 cm, that stage is wrapped up and it's time to push! [learn more](GNS226_U3_T004#GNS226_U3_T004_h4)

question: Which finding in an infant always requires a prompt medical checkup?

options.A: Sneezing once or twice after exposure to morning sunlight
options.B: Spitting up a small amount of milk after a burping session
options.C: A rectal temperature of 38.0°C or higher in a two-month-old
options.D: Having yellow, soft, seedy stools when being breastfed

explanation: Spot on! Any fever in a baby under three months old is an emergency. Always have it checked right away to rule out serious infections. [learn more](GNS324_U3_T12#GNS324_U3_T12_h5)

question: What is considered the first and most fundamental function of nursing management?

options.A: Controlling
options.B: Planning
options.C: Directing
options.D: Staffing

explanation: Planning comes first because it sets the direction and goals before any other management function can take place. [learn more](GST321_U1_T6#GST321_U1_T6_h1)

question: For a rural farming community starting a health fund, when is the best time to collect annual insurance dues?

options.A: Only when a member falls seriously ill
options.B: During harvest seasons when cash flow is highest
options.C: During the dry season when crop failure occurs
options.D: Every single week without exception

explanation: Smart planning! Timing contributions with income cycles makes sure members actually have the cash on hand to pay their dues. [learn more](GST322_U4_T4#GST322_U4_T4_h4)

question: Which of these is an example of a long-acting reversible contraceptive (LARC)?

options.A: Male latex condom
options.B: Spermicidal foam
options.C: Intrauterine device
options.D: Oral contraceptive pill

explanation: An Intrauterine Device (IUD) is placed in the womb and provides protection for years, but can be removed anytime you want. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T46#GNS214_U1_T46_h6)

question: What is the main job of global health funding groups like Gavi or the Global Fund?

options.A: Collecting local taxes from rural market traders to build city hospitals
options.B: Enforcing strict criminal laws against medical malpractice in private clinics
options.C: Directly managing the daily nursing schedules of government health workers
options.D: Pooling resources from multiple sources to buy vaccines and medicines on a large scale

explanation: These global funds collect money from various countries to buy large quantities of essential medicines and vaccines for developing nations. [learn more](GST322_U4_T12#GST322_U4_T12_h3)

question: What is the main focus of palliative care in a residential care home?

options.A: Discharging residents to an acute hospital ward immediately
options.B: Aggressive medical interventions to cure terminal chronic illnesses
options.C: Providing comfort, pain management, and dignity during end-of-life
options.D: Restricting family visits to maintain strict facility quiet hours

explanation: Brilliant! Palliative care is all about comforting patients, easing pain, and giving them dignity when curing is no longer possible. [learn more](GNS324_U5_T12#GNS324_U5_T12_h8)

question: What does 'out-of-pocket health expenditure' mean for an ordinary patient in Nigeria?

options.A: Receiving free medical care funded by international grants
options.B: Paying cash directly to providers at the point of service
options.C: Deducting healthcare costs from monthly cooperative savings
options.D: Using a comprehensive health insurance prepaid card

explanation: Out-of-pocket spending simply means paying cash right there at the hospital counter when you get sick. It's the daily reality for many Nigerians! [learn more](GST322_U4_T3#GST322_U4_T3_h3)

question: What is one of the main responsibilities of community health workers when it comes to post-natal care?

options.A: Performing major surgical repairs for tears
options.B: Delivering babies in primary operating theatres
options.C: Conducting home visits and tracking immunizations
options.D: Prescribing strong antibiotics for severe sepsis

explanation: Community health workers are fantastic bridges to the community. They visit homes to make sure babies get their vaccines and moms are recovering nicely. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T52#GNS214_U1_T52_h9)

question: How do selective media help microbiologists isolate specific microorganisms?

options.A: By changing color every time a fungus touches the plate
options.B: By destroying all living cells present in a water sample
options.C: By allowing certain microbes to grow while stopping the growth of others
options.D: By keeping the Petri dish completely sterile without a lid

explanation: Spot on! Selective media contain special ingredients that block unwanted bacteria so only the specific germ you are looking for can multiply. [learn more](GST114_U5_T2#GST114_U5_T2_h4)

question: What is the primary abnormal type of haemoglobin found in sickle cell anaemia?

options.A: Haemoglobin C
options.B: Haemoglobin F
options.C: Haemoglobin S
options.D: Haemoglobin A

explanation: Sickle cell anaemia is caused by a genetic mutation that produces abnormal haemoglobin S, which distorts red blood cells into a sickle shape when oxygen levels drop. [learn more](GNS311_U2_T7#GNS311_U2_T7_h1)

question: As a psychiatric nurse, why is it so helpful to look beyond a patient's immediate symptoms?

options.A: Because medication orders are written by the hospital pharmacist
options.B: So the patient can be discharged within twenty-four hours
options.C: To diagnose physical infections causing a fever
options.D: To understand the broader ecosystem and life background

explanation: People don't live in a vacuum! Understanding their family, home life, and background helps you see the real root causes of their struggles. [learn more](GNS314_U4_T1#GNS314_U4_T1_h1)

question: What does a low Height-for-Age measurement tell you about a child?

options.A: Temporary weight gain from eating too much sugar
options.B: Acute dehydration from recent diarrhea
options.C: Chronic malnutrition or stunting over a long period
options.D: Immediate lack of protein causing fluid swelling

explanation: Spot on! Height-for-age is our long-term scorecard. A low score tells us the child has been dealing with poor nutrition over a good while (stunting). [learn more](GNS227_U2_T006#GNS227_U2_T006_h6)

question: Which of these is NOT a common feature of end-of-life care in Nigeria?

options.A: Involvement of extended family in medical discussions
options.B: Widespread legal use of formal living wills and advance directives
options.C: Strong influence of Christian and Islamic religious beliefs
options.D: Strict criminal prohibitions against assisted suicide and euthanasia

explanation: While family involvement, religion, and strict laws against euthanasia are very common in Nigeria, formal written living wills are still not widely used or legally integrated into everyday hospital practice yet. [learn more](GNS321_U4_T7#GNS321_U4_T7_h7)

question: What is the biggest hurdle when trying to treat brain tumors using regular systemic chemotherapy drugs?

options.A: Chemotherapy drugs only work on bones and muscles.
options.B: Chemotherapy causes permanent blindness in every patient.
options.C: Brain tissue absorbs too much medication and dissolves instantly.
options.D: The blood-brain barrier blocks many drugs from entering the brain tissue.

explanation: You got it! The blood-brain barrier is like a strict security guard—it protects the brain from toxins, but unfortunately, it also blocks many helpful chemotherapy drugs from getting inside. [learn more](GNS222_U3_T14#GNS222_U3_T14_h5)

question: A patient refuses to look at their surgical scar and covers all mirrors. What is the best nursing action?

options.A: Providing gentle encouragement and a safe space to express body fears
options.B: Ignoring the behavior completely since it is purely cosmetic
options.C: Forcing the patient to look at the wound immediately to build toughness
options.D: Scolding the patient for acting childish about a simple scar

explanation: Patience is key. Empathy and a safe, non-judgmental space help patients process body image trauma at their own speed. [learn more](GNS225_U5_T14#GNS225_U5_T14_h4)

question: What term describes tissue damage caused by a lack of adequate blood supply?

options.A: Ischemia
options.B: Embolism
options.C: Edema
options.D: Hyperemia

explanation: Ischemia is the medical term for inadequate blood flow to a tissue or organ, depriving it of needed oxygen. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T12#GNS111_U2_T12_h8)

question: Why should the vertical axis on a bar chart usually start at zero?

options.A: To make all the bars look exactly the same height
options.B: To hide negative values from the reader
options.C: To prevent exaggerating small differences between groups
options.D: To ensure the chart fits onto a standard notebook page

explanation: Starting at zero maintains correct visual proportions so readers do not misinterpret minor changes as massive clinical differences. [learn more](GNS224_U2_T4#GNS224_U2_T4_h4)

question: Which medication class is most commonly used to reduce severe inflammation inside an arthritic joint?

options.A: Inhaled bronchodilators
options.B: Topical antifungal creams
options.C: Oral loop diuretics
options.D: Corticosteroids

explanation: Corticosteroids are powerful anti-inflammatory drugs frequently injected into joints to calm swelling and pain. [learn more](GNS125_U3_T9#GNS125_U3_T9_h4)

question: A patient undergoing fertility testing shares that she feels deeply sad and worthless. What is the best first thing for a nurse to do?

options.A: Assure her that medical treatments work on the first try for almost everyone
options.B: Tell her that adoption is a very easy alternative to consider right away
options.C: Advise her to stop thinking about pregnancy so her hormones will normalize
options.D: Acknowledge her emotional pain and offer a supportive, non-judgmental space to talk

explanation: You nailed it! Validating her deep emotional pain builds essential trust and shows true compassionate nursing care. Keep up the wonderful work! [learn more](GNS312_U1_T21#GNS312_U1_T21_h6)

question: When can a nurse researcher safely reject the null hypothesis?

options.A: When the calculated p-value is less than or equal to alpha
options.B: When the nursing supervisor demands positive outcomes from the ward
options.C: When the sample size consists of more than ten patients
options.D: When the p-value is much higher than the chosen significance level

explanation: Spot on. When your p-value drops below your set alpha (like 0.05), you have strong enough evidence to say your intervention truly worked! [learn more](GNS217_U4_T15#GNS217_U4_T15_h4)

question: A nurse fills out a Yellow Form for a patient who got a rash after taking two new drugs and an herbal supplement. What should be included in the medication history?

options.A: Only document the drug that the nurse personally administered
options.B: List all prescribed drugs, over-the-counter medications, and herbal products
options.C: Ignore the herbal supplement since it is not a pharmaceutical drug
options.D: Only list the most expensive brand-name prescription drug

explanation: Always list everything! Herbal remedies and over-the-counter items frequently cause or contribute to adverse reactions. [learn more](GNS215_U2_T6#GNS215_U2_T6_h5)

question: When doing nursing research, what are the three main levels used to group literature sources?

options.A: Primary, secondary, and tertiary sources
options.B: Published, unpublished, and grey sources
options.C: Clinical, historical, and theoretical sources
options.D: Qualitative, quantitative, and mixed sources

explanation: You've got this! We group literature into three tiers based on how close the information is to the original study. Primary, secondary, and tertiary keep our research organized. [learn more](GNS217_U3_T6#GNS217_U3_T6_h1)

question: How is the bed arranged when a patient is placed in the Trendelenburg position?

options.A: Head is higher than the feet
options.B: Knees are bent and flat on the mattress
options.C: Head is lower than the feet
options.D: Bed is bent in the middle like a folding chair

explanation: In Trendelenburg, the whole bed tilts so the patient's head is lower than their feet. Gravity helps blood flow to the brain! [learn more](GNS112_U4_T8#GNS112_U4_T8_h5)

question: How should you handle your personal moral beliefs when caring for a post-abortion client?

options.A: Refuse to provide any medication or comfort
options.B: Put personal views aside to deliver respectful care
options.C: Report the client to religious leaders
options.D: Argue with the client about their life choices

explanation: Professional nursing ethics mean we always put our patient's health and dignity first, delivering unbiased, compassionate care no matter our personal background. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T007#GNS226_U5_T007_h2)

question: Why must metformin be withheld from patients receiving an iodine contrast agent?

options.A: To stop the contrast dye from crystallizing inside the stomach lining
options.B: To keep the patient's blood pressure from dropping too low during the test
options.C: To prevent the dangerous buildup of lactic acidosis if kidneys struggle
options.D: To ensure the x-ray machine captures a clear picture of the pancreas

explanation: If the contrast temporarily impairs kidney function, metformin can accumulate and trigger a severe metabolic complication called lactic acidosis. [learn more](GNS213_U4_T3#GNS213_U4_T3_h3)

question: In tracheostomy care, what does the term 'decannulation' mean?

options.A: Permanent removal of the tracheostomy tube
options.B: Inserting a new mechanical ventilation machine
options.C: Inflating the cuff to maximum pressure
options.D: Cleaning the inner cannula with sterile water

explanation: Decannulation simply means the tube is finally and permanently removed because the patient no longer needs it. You're mastering the terminology! [learn more](GNS213_U2_T14#GNS213_U2_T14_h6)

question: What is the key difference between Acute Stress Disorder and Post-Traumatic Stress Disorder?

options.A: Whether the patient has physical injuries or not
options.B: The time frame and duration of the symptoms
options.C: The age of the person experiencing the trauma
options.D: The specific type of disaster that caused the trauma

explanation: Acute Stress Disorder happens shortly after the event, whereas PTSD involves long-lasting symptoms that persist over months or years. [learn more](GNS315_U5_T6#GNS315_U5_T6_h3)

question: How does severe kidney disease affect how medications act in the body?

options.A: It immediately destroys the drug inside the stomach.
options.B: It prevents the drug from ever entering the bloodstream.
options.C: It delays drug clearance and causes dangerous accumulation.
options.D: It turns all medications into inactive sugar compounds.

explanation: Since the kidneys act like the body's filter, disease makes it hard for them to clear out drugs. This causes the medicine to pile up to unsafe levels. [learn more](GNS125_U5_T5#GNS125_U5_T5_h7)

question: Which healthcare professional should you team up with when a patient has trouble chewing or swallowing?

options.A: Speech-language pathologist
options.B: Hospital administrative clerk
options.C: Physical rehabilitation trainer
options.D: Biochemical laboratory technician

explanation: Speech therapists are experts at assessing swallowing disorders and helping patients eat safely. Teamwork makes the dream work! [learn more](GNS227_U5_T004#GNS227_U5_T004_h7)

question: Why is spotting patient risks early considered a protective action?

options.A: It guarantees the patient will never experience an infection
options.B: It allows nurses to build barriers against potential hazards
options.C: It removes all clinical responsibilities from the doctor
options.D: It stops patients from moving around the ward

explanation: Spotting risks beforehand lets you put preventative steps in place before an accident or complication actually happens. You've got this! [learn more](GNS122_U3_T8#GNS122_U3_T8_h1)

question: What happens when someone consistently eats fewer calories than they burn?

options.A: The basal metabolic rate increases to compensate for lack of food
options.B: The digestive system shuts down completely to conserve water
options.C: The body breaks down stored fat and tissue to make up the deficit
options.D: The liver immediately converts the calorie shortage into new bone

explanation: If there's a calorie gap, the body gets resourceful—it dips into stored fat and muscle to find the energy it needs. [learn more](GNS227_U1_T010#GNS227_U1_T010_h7)

question: Which of these is NOT a common challenge faced by NGOs working in Nigeria?

options.A: Cultural resistance and suspicion from community elders
options.B: Heavy reliance on unstable international donor grants
options.C: Excessive, guaranteed long-term funding from secure local taxes
options.D: Insecure terrain and poor rural road networks

explanation: NGOs don't collect taxes! In fact, relying on unpredictable donor grants is one of their biggest headaches, not a guaranteed income. [learn more](GNS225_U5_T27#GNS225_U5_T27_h6)

question: What happens when Cooper's ligaments stretch or lose their elasticity?

options.A: Milk production stops completely
options.B: New glandular lobes form
options.C: The areola changes color
options.D: The breasts begin to sag

explanation: Because these ligaments provide structural support against gravity, their stretching leads to a natural sagging appearance. [learn more](GNS121_U5_T16#GNS121_U5_T16_h5)

question: Which type of exercise involves the nurse moving the joints of a patient who cannot move at all?

options.A: Passive exercises
options.B: Resistive exercises
options.C: Active exercises
options.D: Active-assistive exercises

explanation: When a patient cannot move their limbs themselves, you step in and gently move their joints for them. That is what passive exercises are all about! [learn more](GNS221_U1_T4#GNS221_U1_T4_h2)

question: What is the main goal of Mass Drug Administration (MDA) programs in communities with high worm rates?

options.A: Reducing the overall parasite burden across the entire population
options.B: Eliminating the need for basic sanitation and clean water supply
options.C: Curating permanent immunity against all bacterial and viral pathogens
options.D: Diagnosing individual complex surgical emergencies in local hospitals

explanation: MDA treats whole communities at once to quickly bring down the total number of worms and stop heavy transmission without needing individual lab tests. [learn more](GST114_U3_T6#GST114_U3_T6_h9)

question: Which transmission route involves living creatures, like mosquitoes, carrying a pathogen to a human?

options.A: Fomite contamination
options.B: Direct droplet spread
options.C: Airborne suspension
options.D: Vector-borne transmission

explanation: Spot on! Vectors are living taxis for germs—mostly insects like mosquitoes and ticks that shuttle pathogens right to us. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T2#GNS313_U1_T2_h5)

question: What does 'cross-contamination' mean in a kitchen setting?

options.A: The transfer of harmful pathogens from one surface or food to another
options.B: The chemical reaction that occurs when mixing two different spices
options.C: The freezing of fresh vegetables at incorrect freezer temperatures
options.D: The natural spoilage of food caused by exposure to direct sunlight

explanation: Spot on! Cross-contamination happens when germs travel from a dirty source (like raw meat) over to safe food (like a fresh salad). [learn more](GNS227_U3_T009#GNS227_U3_T009_h4)

question: Why should newly hired nurses be introduced to the hospital's cultural values during orientation?

options.A: To discourage them from asking senior staff members for clinical help
options.B: To ensure they adopt expected behaviours and maintain the positive environment
options.C: To test their ability to memorize complex hospital administration bylaws
options.D: To reduce the amount of orientation salary the hospital has to pay them

explanation: Spot on! Early orientation helps new nurses fit right into the positive workplace culture, keeping standards of teamwork and safety high. [learn more](GST319_U6_T7#GST319_U6_T7_h7)

question: An 80-year-old patient with mild nerve numbness in their hands (neuropathy) is going home. Which safety change is most important?

options.A: Placing heavy glass mugs on the lowest possible counter shelf
options.B: Removing all rugs to prevent tripping and broken bones
options.C: Installing an automatic shut-off timer on the kitchen stove
options.D: Buying a brighter desk lamp for reading in the evening

explanation: You got it! Since neuropathy reduces feeling in the hands, an automatic stove timer prevents them from accidentally leaving burners on or misjudging hot pots. [learn more](GNS324_U6_T6#GNS324_U6_T6_h5)

question: Why is amenorrhoea best thought of as a warning sign rather than a disease on its own?

options.A: It always resolves on its own without any medical treatment
options.B: It cannot be measured with standard laboratory blood tests
options.C: It only happens during normal life stages like pregnancy
options.D: It is a symptom caused by an underlying physical or hormonal problem

explanation: Just like a fever, amenorrhoea is your body's way of telling you that something else is throwing off its normal hormone balance. [learn more](GNS216_U2_T4#GNS216_U2_T4_h1)

question: Why do vulnerable or socially excluded patients often delay going to the hospital when sick?

options.A: They fear mistreatment, discrimination, or face overwhelming financial and social barriers
options.B: Government policies legally forbid them from entering primary health centers
options.C: They lack any physical symptoms of illness until disease is terminal
options.D: They prefer traditional remedies exclusively over modern clinical treatments

question: A nursing mother complains of sharp nipple pain and visible cracks. What should you as a nurse check first?

options.A: Suggest weaning the baby to formula immediately
options.B: Recommend applying strong antiseptic ointments before every feed
options.C: Assess the infant's latch technique and mouth positioning during feeding
options.D: Advise the mother to stop breastfeeding completely for one week

question: Why must breastfeeding mothers make sure they drink plenty of extra fluids every day?

options.B: To flush out the kidneys and stop weight gain
options.C: To help the lochia turn white faster
options.D: To prevent the uterus from contracting too fast

question: Why is it often so hard to enforce anti-FGM laws at the local community level?

options.A: Federal laws completely override all state and local police actions

options.C: Medical doctors are required by law to perform the procedure instead
options.D: Cultural secrecy and fear of ostracization prevent people from reporting cases

question: On a busy hospital ward, what is the most common reason medication preparation errors happen?

options.B: Pharmacies sending drugs in alphabetical order
options.C: Lack of basic mathematical formulas in textbooks
options.D: Distractions and interruptions during the setup process

question: What do plant 'secondary metabolites' mainly do for the plant and for medicine?

options.C: Storing plain water during heavy droughts
options.D: Providing basic structural cellulose for the stem

question: What is moulding in the context of labour?

options.C: The abnormal swelling of the baby's scalp caused by pressure

question: What is the very first thing you should do when facing an ethical dilemma at a patient's home?

question: Why do symptoms only show up a year after a person first gets infected?

question: What do we call it when a nurse dumps way too many duties onto assistants, making safe care impossible?

options.B: Reverse supervision
options.C: Clinical autonomy
options.D: Under-delegation

question: Why are humans considered accidental or dead-end hosts for this parasite?

question: Which of the following is an example of a social determinant of health?

options.D: The brand of medication prescribed by a doctor
